sections.text:
In a beautiful forest, there was a sly fox who loved to tell practical jokes and make fun of other animals.

One day, the fox decided to make fun of the stork, which had a very long beak and thin, thin legs.

The fox went to the stork and said to him with feigned kindness: “My friend, the stork, we have not seen each other for a while. How about you kindly accept my invitation to have dinner at my house tonight? I have prepared a very delicious soup!”

The kind stork was delighted with this friendly invitation and accepted it with pleasure.

In the evening, the stork arrived at the fox's house, very hungry and ready to eat the delicious, fragrant soup.

The fox welcomed the stork, then brought dinner, and here the cunning trick began!
The fox poured the very delicious soup into two completely flat plates (like the plates in which pancakes are served), and placed them on the table.

The fox said slyly: “Come in, my friend, eat until you’re satisfied!”

The fox began licking the soup from the flat plate with his broad tongue quickly and easily until he finished his entire plate.

As for the poor stork, his beak was long, thin, and sharp, and whenever he tried to eat soup from the flat dish, his beak could not catch any drop, and the beak would hit the bottom of the dish with an annoying sound.

The stork felt very hungry and embarrassed, while the fox looked at him, laughing sarcastically in his secret, saying: “Oh! You don’t seem to like the soup, my friend? It’s okay, I’ll eat it so it doesn’t spoil!”

The stork realized that the fox had invited him just to make fun of him, but he did not show his anger. Rather, he smiled calmly and said before leaving: “Thank you for this wonderful dinner, fox. Please accept my invitation to have dinner at my house next week so that we can return this generosity to you.”

The fox happily agreed, he loves eating free food.

The next week, the fox went to the stork's house, and he was very hungry and salivating at the delicious smell of roasted meat.

The stork welcomed the fox and said: “Come, my friend. I have prepared for you a meal of minced meat seasoned with the most delicious spices!”

Here, the stork brought food.

But he put it in two very long jars with a very thin neck and a narrow opening like a flute!
The stork easily inserted his long, thin beak into the jar, and began eating the delicious meat, enjoying it until he was completely satisfied.

As for the fox, he tried to put his wide mouth into the narrow opening of the jar, but he could not!
He tried to lick from the outside, but did not achieve anything. He tried to insert his hand, but it was wider than the opening!
All the fox could do was just lick the outside of the glass jar and smell the delicious smell, which increased his hunger insanely.

The stork looked at the fox coldly and said: “Oh! You don’t seem to like the meat, my fox friend?”

The fox felt extremely embarrassed and ashamed, and realized that he had fallen into the evil of his deeds, and that the stork had taught him a lesson in the same cunning way.

The fox returned to his home hungry and humiliated, and he was not angry with the stork, because he knew that what he did to him was just, and that whoever deceives people should expect that they will deceive him in the same way, and as you condemn, you will be condemned.
